The problem here is the localization is defined in the Core project. Actually, it's something related to presentation. We did it like that to allow you to use localization code in application and domain layers too.

title: Execute logic right after user logged in
body:
We need to integrate with a third party web application. They provide an endpoint to generate tokens that are then used to access their APIs and pages.
We want to call their generate tokens endpoint right after a Login in our app.

I thought of raising an event in the AccountController, right after the SignInAsync() has completed.
The event is raised and received by my handler ok. However, if I inject an AbpSession in my handler, the UserId is still null, it seems the abp session is not yet fully initialized.
Is that expected behavior ?

The other approach I was thinking of was to make a call to an ApplicationService from the javascript, right after the user logged in.
However, i can't find any client side hook where i know the user just logged in.
Any ideas ?

Thanks!
author: guilmori

comments.body: Pass `loginResult.User.Id` in your event data.

Just after user login, you can not reach to AbpSession.UserId in the same request, because AspNet MVC does not set user to HttpContext.User yet. You obtain UserId on login and pass it to your event as @acjh said.

For client side, return UserId from login ajax call, so you will have UserId that can be directly used.

On server side, I could pass the UserId as parameter, but then my handler could make use of other components that depends on AbpSession, so this is not reliable enough.

On the client side, I want to execute code only after a login, where should I hook my code ? 
My Login form dates of old ABP version, it is a simple razor view that submits the form to the Account Controller, then the Account controller issue a redirect on successful login. There is no ajax call. 

I will try to download a new ABP solution and check if the updated version has more hook point.

For client side, I suggest you to seperate login from other actions. That means you refresh page after login so after refreshing you will see that user has logged in (abp.session.userId has a value) in the client side.

I had tried the `Use` method, but it ended in a not implemented exception. I will try again with more recent ABP version.

For client side, i may not understand you correctly. I want to execute my code only right after a login. So I don't want my code to execute when for example the user refresh the browser page, and is already logged in.

Finally the `AbpSession.Use()` method worked. So I'm gonna initiate my logic server side for now.

title: the different design-pattern to design SettingProvider or IXXManager
body:
sorry for I couldn't quite accurately describe my problems.
I am confused with SettingProvider which was designed like abstract class and Manager which was designed like interface. could you provider some tips? Or what's your intention.
author: panchengtao

comments.body:
For IxxxManager interface and xxxManager implementation pairs: It's a good separation for unit tests. There are no abstract base xxxManagers generally, since we don't expect that you replace those managers. Even if you replace them, you can derive from the manager itself, which is a concrete class.

SettingProvider could be an interface, don't have a good reason. I just thought that I can add some base methods in the future, but I hadn't add yet.

thanks a lot, I really appreciate it. by a way, would you mind giving me a few pointers with your consideration when you design an interface or an abstract class. I often feel confused with those problem

Actually, this is not unique to ABP and you can find good articles on the web. That depends on your requirements and classes.
For a domain service/manager, I suggest interface+implementation since it allows you to replace it in unit tests, but in real application you will generally have a single implementation.

If you think that you have more than one implementation for an interface, we generally use this pattern:

````
interface IYourService
abstract class YourServiceBase : IYourService
class YourServiceImpl1 : YourServiceBase
class YourServiceImpl2 : YourServiceBase
````
This provides flexibility. A new implementation can directly implement IYourService or derive from YourServiceBase.
YourServiceBase generally include common base functionality, like template class pattern.

But, it's hard to say a general rule for all cases, it depends on your case.

title: webapi without ajax occurred csrf
body:
I an using webapi for exporting excel (return HttpResponseMessage ), client is post; Then it notice me antiforgerytoken validation error, even I added @Html.AntiForgeryToken()  into the form.  so I could only add [DisableAbpAntiForgeryTokenValidation] on it.

What's another idea for solving the problem?
author: WilCameronP

comments.body:
Check browser's network tab to see if anti forgery token is sent.
I didn't understand it well, did DisableAbpAntiForgeryTokenValidation solve the problem?

It's because Web API can not recognize form values. It expects antiforgery token be sent in the header.
If you would make an ajax call, ABP automatically adds it to the header. But in a non-ajax request, it can not do it.
In MVC, it's possible, because MVC can better handle form values. But Web API is designed to bind HTTP body to model and we can not directly get antiforgery token from form like MVC.
I suggest you to make it via an MVC action rather than a Web API, if possible. Otherwise, you should handle anti forgery manually.
I think I got it. Thanks a lot

comments.body:
Hi,

Call Release whenever it's possible. As better, use ResolveAsDisposable in a using statement.
But.. if your resolving object is Singleton.. then releasing has no effect actually. So, you may not call Release in that case. But call Release even in that case wherever it's possible (you may change Singleton to Transient in the future, for example).

comments.body:
Hi, This is about lazy load of EF. Alternative solutions: 1. You can make GetLocationMappings method virtual, like: 
public virtual GetLocationMappingsOutput GetLocationMappings(GetLocationMappingsInput aInput)
Thus, ABP can implement UOW for this method, and session will be usable in this method. If you did use this class over an interface, it was not needed. This works but also implement 2nd solution: 1. You can select LocationMappingTableModel included Countries. This is better than 1st solution (Actually, you should make it virtual anyway). Because, in first solution, EF will make a db query for each contry and this is a performance killer. This known as N+1 problem. When you Include Contries, it will execute just one query. To implement it, You can add a method to your repository named GetAllListWithCountries() and in that like this: 
return GetAll().Include(l => l.Country).ToList();
If you have added referenced to EntityFramework nuget package to your application layer and made GetLocationMappings virtual, then you can replace this line: List locationMappings = _LocationMappingRepository.GetAllList(); wtih this one: List locationMappings = _LocationMappingRepository.GetAll().Include(l => l.Country).ToList();; Thus, you don't need to create a new repository method.

I also have some advices:
- EmEntityCommon and EmEntityBase classes should be abstract as I understand.
- LocationMappingTableModel is not a good name. Why do you postfix with TableModel? If you want to implement DDD, your entities are Entity, not table model. LocationMapping is enough. If you really like, LocationMappingEntity is better. But if you dont want to implement DDD, it's OK.
- Your GetLocationMappings method can be much more smaller if you map LocationMappingTableModel  to LocationMappingDto. AutoMapper can do nested mappings.

Thanks for using it :)
